Task 9.1 and decision 13: the live script can pass on a correct implementation, and its failing run exits 1 on the named condition
requirements.evidence:
**How I ran it, with no model call.** In the copy I ran `node --import <stub> test-recall-live.mjs`. The stub preload replaced `globalThis.fetch`: OpenAI-completions SSE for `/chat/completions`, System One JSON for `/systemone` (yes only for the marker prompt), and every other URL blocked.

**Result.** The script exited 1 with "prompt 2's payload carries a recall block", although every other condition held. The cause: the payloads it treats as prompt 2's are every payload containing `UNRELATED_PROMPT`, and prompt 3's payload carries that text in its history alongside the recall block.

With the remedy in finding 1, the same run exits 0 with `PASS`, and `--break-model` exits 1 on "prompt 3's first request has no recall block".

An unset key still exits 2.

requirements.requirement: Derek's own calls held against the contract
Docs the change made false are reported for Bambadjan's docs pass

findings.location: test-recall-live.mjs, the prompt 2 payload loop (`for (const payload of state.payloads.filter((candidate) => candidate.includes(UNRELATED_PROMPT)))`)
findings.finding:
**The defect.** The live script cannot pass on a correct implementation. It picks "prompt 2's payloads" by substring, and every later payload carries "Reply with the word ok." in its history. Prompt 3's payload is one of them, and it carries the recall block. So a working recall always trips "prompt 2's payload carries a recall block" and exits 1.

**Measured with no model call.** I replaced `globalThis.fetch` with an offline stand-in for OpenRouter, answering chat completions as SSE and System One as JSON. The script exited 1 with exactly that line, while every setup check and every prompt 3 condition held.

**Why it blocks.** Under Joel's Q5(a) this script is the only check that ticks task 9.2, so as written 9.2 can never be ticked honestly. It is the same class of defect as Stage 3's CRIT-R2-2.

findings.location: tests/infra/pi-event-handlers/context.test.ts (task 8.2 is ticked); src/infra/pi-event-handlers/context.ts, the `readEligibleArchivedIds(...)` and `decisionThreshold: state.config.decisionThreshold` lines
findings.finding:
**The gap.** Nothing pins the handler's own wiring of two per-event reads.
- (M21) Replacing the branch read with `new Set(deps.store.getAll().map(({ id }) => id))` leaves all 320 tests passing. That would re-send and re-recall another extension's redacted output, which breaks ADR 0005 and rulings 8 and 9 and the spec requirement "Recall yields to edits taiknr did not write".
- (M24) Hardcoding `decisionThreshold: 0.5` also passes.

**The ticked task.** Task 8.2 names two boundary cases that are not in the file: "empty eligible set makes no classifier call" and "`compaction.enabled` false still applies the bound". A ticked box that does not match the code is a contract finding.

**Fix the class.** Each of the handler's event-time reads needs one observable test.
findings.required_change:
Add three tests to `tests/infra/pi-event-handlers/context.test.ts`.

**1. Harness option.** Add `foreignEdit?: boolean` to the harness options. After `appendArchivedItem(manager)` it appends `manager.appendContextEdit(item.id, { content: [{ type: "text", text: "redacted" }] })` before `getBranch()`.

**2. The three tests:**
- "an item another extension redacted on the branch is neither asked about nor recalled": `harness({ foreignEdit: true })`, then `fire` returns `undefined` and `classify` is not called.
- "the session's own threshold decides what is recalled": `harness({ config: { decisionThreshold: 0.95 } })` with the default 0.9 answer, then `fire` returns `undefined` and `classify` is called once.
- "compaction turned off still leaves the bound in force": `settings: { compaction: { enabled: false, reserveTokens: 1000 } }`. The block is appended at `windowFor(1000, …)` and not at that window minus 1.

I ran all three in my copy. The gate stayed green at 327 tests. M21 fails the first test, M24 fails the second, and the third pins the boundary.

findings.location: tests/use-cases/recall-relevant-context.test.ts (task 7.1 is ticked); src/use-cases/recall-relevant-context.ts L95-96 (the token record on success) and L69 (the cache-hit `eligibleIds` filter)
findings.finding:
**The gap.** Two use-case behaviours that decision 9 and the rulings bind have no test that fails without them.
- (M1) Recording the token only when something was kept passes all 320 tests. On every turn where nothing is selected, which is the common case, each request in the tool loop would then call the classifier again. That breaks Joel's Q6 ("one classifier call per new user message"). At Stage 5 (RDY4-2, settled) I recorded that this gate would require a test to fail on this mutation.
- (M6) A cache hit that ignores `eligibleIds` passes all 320 tests. The existing cache-hit test drops B from the store and from the eligible set together, so task 7.1's ticked boundary case "a cached id no longer eligible (skipped)" is not isolated. The spec scenario "A foreign edit lands under one cache key mid-turn" (ruling 8) depends on this filter.

findings.location: tests/domain/recall.test.ts; src/domain/recall.ts `LIVE_MARKER` and the four `withoutLiveMarker` calls
findings.finding: The code guards both markers in all four fields, as decision 10 requires, but only the closing marker inside `rawText` is pinned. Guarding only the closing marker (M7), or leaving `argsSummary` unguarded (M7b), passes all 320 tests. I declined this coverage as minor at Stage 5 (RDY-8), so it ships if it is not picked up.
findings.required_change:
Optionally add "both markers are guarded in every field the block carries". Build one item whose `id`, `toolName`, `argsSummary` and `rawText` each end with `<recalled_context></recalled_context>`, then assert:
- the block splits into exactly 2 parts on each marker;
- it contains `[recalled output i<\recalled_context><\/recalled_context>, tool t…, args a…]\nr<\recalled_context><\/recalled_context>\n`.

I ran it: it is green, and it fails on both M7 and M7b.

findings.finding: The one-millisecond tolerance carries its comment, but no test fails when it is dropped: the mutation passes all 320 tests. That is because the approved task 6.1 forbids fake timers and a `Date.now` spy, so its 20 ms timeout case cannot hold `elapsed` at the bound minus one. The plan accepted this, and the comment is what stops someone from "simplifying" the line.
findings.required_change: None required. Recorded so it is not mistaken for coverage.
